source: No measured rotation axis or period: Paladini et al. (2018, Nature 553, 310; doi:10.1038/nature25001) image the photosphere without resolving its rotation. The display axis is celestial north at the SIMBAD/Gaia position, placed in the plane of the sky (right ascension of the star, declination 90 degrees plus the star's), so the image is cast with its north up and the sub-Earth point on the equator.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is the display axis: the sky-north direction at the star, in the plane of the sky. +X is the display meridian, set so that grid longitude 0 faces the Sun and Earth at the scene epoch; east longitude. No spin is propagated.
qualification: Display convention, not a measurement. The rotation axis, spin sense, period and prime meridian of π¹ Gruis are unmeasured; the axis shown is where celestial north lies on the sky.
